To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a pHEMT-based low-noise amplifier (LNA) for VSAT applications has a better noise figure and a lower power consumption than a GaAs MESFET LNA at 8 GHz, but it has a higher gain at room temperature.
the noise figure and gain of a pHEMT LNA for a VSAT receiver system are strongly dependent upon temperature and frequency.

a LNA design based on a 0.25 μm GaAs pHEMT technology, with a noise temperature of 50 K at 10 GHz, can be realized with a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 6 GHz, and a 1 dB compression point of +15 dBm, with a power consumption of less than 100 mW.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low-noise amplifiers (LNA) for VSAT receivers operating in the 8–16 GHz frequency band.
the design and characterization of the low noise amplifier, a key component for satellite communications.

the development of a low noise amplifier for VSAT applications, with the following features: - Low cost and high yield - Low noise - High linearity - High gain - Low power consumption - Low temperature sensitivity The LNA design will be based on a pseudomorphic HEPIT (pHEMT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LNA is able to operate at the lowest possible temperatures (i.e. down to -50 ° C) and at the highest possible frequencies (i.e. above 10 GHz).
, for the considered VSAT receiver system, the best trade-off between noise figure and power gain is achieved at room temperature.
the performance of a pHEMT-based LNA for a VSAT receiver application is strongly dependent on temperature and frequency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a LNA design for VSAT applications has to be carefully optimized in terms of noise figure and power dissipation, taking into account both the temperature and frequency dependence of the pHemt parameters, in order to obtain the best performance.
the LNA noise performance degrades as the temperature decreases, while the power gain increases.

the temperature dependence of the LNA gain is more important than its noise figure, while the input and output matching networks have to be optimized to achieve a good performance at both low and room temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LNA performance is strongly temperature dependent.
the noise figure is the most critical performance parameter, and the temperature dependence is more pronounced at lower frequency.
the LNA performance is not significantly affected by the temperature variations, which makes the LNA suitable for VSAT applications.
